passage.title: The Island That Grew
paras: In November 1963, a fishing boat was sailing off the south coast of Iceland when the crew noticed something strange. A column of dark smoke was rising from the sea. At first they thought another boat was on fire. They were wrong.

Deep under the water, a volcano was erupting. Hot, melted rock called lava was pouring out of the sea floor. When it met the cold water, it hissed and exploded into clouds of steam and ash. Day after day, the rock piled higher until, at last, it rose above the waves. A brand-new island had been born.

The island was named Surtsey, after a fire giant from old Icelandic stories. The eruptions carried on for more than three years. By the time they stopped in 1967, the island was about 2.7 square kilometres in size.

Scientists were delighted. Here was a chance to watch how life arrives on bare, new land. They decided that only a few scientists would be allowed to visit, so that people would not bring seeds or insects by accident.

Life came anyway. Seeds floated in on the sea and were dropped by birds. The first plant was found in 1965. Seabirds began to nest on the cliffs, and their droppings made the ground richer. Today, dozens of kinds of plants grow there.

But Surtsey is slowly shrinking. Wind and waves wear away its soft rock, and one day it may disappear beneath the sea again. Until then, it remains one of the most special places on Earth: an island that grew.

questions.q: When was the first plant found?

questions.a: They could watch how life arrives on bare, new land

questions.q: Summarise the passage in one sentence.
questions.a: A volcano made a new island near Iceland in 1963, and plants and birds slowly arrived, though it is now shrinking.
